cards.text: The prophet Isaiah opens this message like the LOUDEST alarm clock on earth: 'Awake, awake!' He's calling Jerusalem, the city of God's people, to rise up. She has drunk a cup from the hand of the LORD, and friend, she is NOT doing well.

cards.question: Jerusalem drank a cup from the hand of the LORD. What was in it?
Jerusalem took one sip from the cup of the LORD's fury and set it down.

cards.text: She drained that goblet to the dregs, and it's the cup that makes men stagger. So now she's staggering, and she has sons she bore and brought up.

cards.question: Jerusalem is staggering. Among all the sons she brought up, how many are there to take her hand?

cards.text: Then the prophet lists what has hit her, and it comes in pairs: devastation and destruction, famine and sword. And he asks, 'Who will grieve for you? Who can comfort you?'
Her sons? They've fainted, and they lie at the head of every street. The prophet compares them to an antelope.

cards.question: The prophet says Jerusalem's fainted sons are like an antelope caught in what?
The prophet says Jerusalem's fainted sons are full of the wrath of the LORD.

cards.text: Then the prophet says, 'Therefore now hear this, you afflicted one, drunken, but not with wine.' Staggering down the street and not ONE drop of wine, friend, so that's how strong that cup is.
Then the prophet passes along what the LORD says, and he calls Him 'your Lord, the LORD, even your God, who defends His people.' Lean in, friend, because here comes the turn.

cards.question: The LORD who defends His people sees the cup of staggering in Jerusalem's hand. What does He do with it?
The LORD tells Jerusalem she will drink from the cup of His fury again one day.

cards.text: Never again. But that cup doesn't just vanish into thin air, because the LORD has somewhere else in mind for it.

cards.question: The LORD takes the cup of His fury from Jerusalem. Whose hands does He place it in?
What did Jerusalem's tormentors tell her?

answers.text: Lie down so we can walk over you
Bow down to our gods every day
Leave this city and never return

cards.text: So she made her back like the ground, like a street for them to walk on. And I thought years under a stack of takeout menus in a junk drawer was rough.

That wake-up call again, friend, 'Awake, awake,' and there's no snooze button on this one. This time the prophet calls Jerusalem Zion and the holy city, and he tells her to clothe herself with strength.

cards.question: Strength isn't the only thing the prophet tells Jerusalem to put on. What else?
The prophet says the uncircumcised and unclean will keep coming into Jerusalem, the holy city.

cards.text: Then: 'Shake off your dust! Rise up and sit on your throne, O Jerusalem.' Friend, I wore a whole COAT of dust in that junk drawer for years, and nobody ever told me to go sit on a throne.

cards.question: The prophet calls Jerusalem the captive Daughter of Zion. What does he tell her to remove from her neck?

cards.text: Then the LORD says she was sold for nothing. NOTHING, friend, and I went for 25 cents at a bakery closing sale thinking I was the bargain of the century.

cards.question: The LORD says Jerusalem was sold for nothing. How does He say she will be redeemed?

cards.text: Then the Lord GOD looks back at how His people got here, one place at a time.

cards.question: At first God's people went down to ___ to live, then ___ oppressed them without cause.

cards.text: And now? The LORD says His people have been taken without cause, and those who rule them taunt. On top of that, He says His name is blasphemed continually all day long.

cards.question: The LORD's name is blasphemed all day long. Therefore, what does He say His people will know?
The LORD says that on that day, His people will know that He is the One who speaks.

cards.text: And then the LORD says it plainly: 'Here I am!' Three words, friend, so let them sit a minute.
Now the prophet turns our eyes to the mountains. Messengers are coming over them, the ones who bring good news and proclaim peace and salvation. And they have something to say to Zion.

cards.question: The messengers on the mountains bring good news. What do they say to Zion?
The prophet says the feet of those who bring good news are beautiful.

cards.text: Beautiful FEET, friend, and I'm a guy who stands on a gold base, so I'm not judging anybody. Then the watchmen lift up their voices and shout for joy together.

cards.question: Why are Zion's watchmen shouting for joy?

cards.text: Then the prophet tells the ruins of Jerusalem to break forth in joy and sing together. Ruins that SING, friend, and that's not a city getting back on its feet, that's a city getting back on its feet and doing a little dance.

cards.question: Why do the ruins of Jerusalem break forth in joy?

answers.text: The LORD has comforted His people

cards.text: And the prophet says the LORD has bared His holy arm in the sight of all the nations. Sleeves UP, friend, and everybody's watching.

cards.question: The LORD bares His holy arm in the sight of all the nations. Who will see the salvation of our God?

answers.text: All the ends of the earth

cards.text: Then a new call: 'Depart, depart, go out from there!' Believe me, friend, I know what it's like to hear that it's finally time to get out.

cards.question: As they go out, what does the prophet tell them not to touch?
Who does the prophet tell to purify themselves as they go out?

answers.text: Those who carry the vessels of the LORD
Those who guard the city walls
Those who rebuild the city ruins

cards.text: Then the prophet tells them how this exit is going to go.

cards.question: The prophet says they will leave in a hurry and flee in haste.

cards.text: No running out the door with one shoe on. The prophet says the LORD goes before them.

cards.question: The LORD goes before them as they leave. Who is their rear guard?

cards.text: God in front, God in back. When I got called out of the junk drawer, ONE angel showed up, and I thought THAT was the VIP treatment.

findings.problem: The answer (an antelope in a net) is a detail of the picture that the baker cannot reason out. A net, a thicket and a pit are all equally believable traps, and nothing on earlier cards points to a net. The only way to get it right is luck. The question also tests a small wording detail instead of what the picture means.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences. It isn't the opening card of the walkthrough, so it can have at most 2.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The setup gives the answer away. Card 8 ends with 'everybody's watching', and the question itself says 'in the sight of all the nations'. Together they rule out 'Only the watchmen' and 'Only the people of Zion', so 'All the ends of the earth' is obvious.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The question says 'As they go out' without saying who 'they' are. The earlier story card isn't on screen, and no card has said who is being told to depart.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.
